﴿فنقبوا في البلاد هل من محيص﴾: فنقبوا: the fāʾ is a conjunction; نقبوا: a verb and its fāʿil; the conjoining is according to the meaning, as though: "their might grew strong, so they roamed"; في البلاد: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿نقبوا﴾; هل: an interrogative particle; من: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; محيص: genitive in wording, nominative in position as a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being omitted, its implied form being "لهم" ("for them") or "لغيرهم" ("for others"); the clause هل من محيص is the object of an omitted saying, and the clause of saying is a ḥāl from the wāw of نقبوا, i.e. "so they roamed through the lands, saying: is there any escape?".

muyesser-irab:37-37.t: ﴿إن في ذلك لذكرى لمن كان له قلب أو ألقى السمع وهو شهيد﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); في ذلك: the fronted khabar (predicate) of إن; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; ذكرى: the noun of إن; لمن: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of ذكرى; the clause كان is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. له: the fronted khabar of كان; قلب: its postponed noun; أو: a conjunction particle; ألقى السمع: a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); هو: mubtadaʾ (subject); شهيد: khabar.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿ولقد خلقنا السماوات والأرض وما بينهما في ستة أيام﴾: the wāw is resumptive; the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; قد: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); خلقنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); السماوات: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الأرض is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السماوات; في ستة أيام: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلقنا; the clause ﴿ولقد خلقنا السماوات...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿وما مسنا من لغوب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ما: negative; مسنا: a past verb, and نا is mafʿūl bihi; من: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; لغوب: genitive in wording, nominative in position because it is the fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿فاصبر على ما يقولون﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition); اصبر: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you"; على ما يقولون: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اصبر﴾.
﴿وسبح بحمد ربك﴾: سبح: an imperative verb; بحمد ربك: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of سبح, i.e. "pray, praising".
﴿قبل طلوع الشمس﴾: an adverb attached to سبح.
﴿وقبل الغروب﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the adverb.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿قد علمنا ما تنقص الأرض منهم وعندنا كتاب حفيظ﴾: a resumptive statement with no grammatical position; قد: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); علمنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); ما: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿تنقص الأرض﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. منهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تنقص; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); عندنا: an adverb attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); كتاب: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); حفيظ: an adjective; and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:40-40.t: ﴿ومن الليل فسبحه وأدبار السجود﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من الليل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبح; the fāʾ is a conjunction; سبحه: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); أدبار السجود: an adverb.

muyesser-irab:41-41.t: ﴿واستمع يوم يناد المناد من مكان قريب﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes; استمع: an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "you", and its object omitted, i.e. "and listen to the call of the caller"; the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿استمع﴾. And it has been said: the implied object is "what I tell you", in which case يوم is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied ﴿يخرجون﴾ indicated by His words; المناد: fāʿil; من مكان: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ينادي﴾; قريب: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:42-42.t: ﴿يوم يسمعون الصيحة بالحق ذلك يوم الخروج﴾: the adverb is a badal (substitute) from the first adverb; the clause يسمعون is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the annexation of إذا to it [Translator's note: so in the source; the adverb here is ﴿يوم﴾, not إذا]; الصيحة: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بالحق: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the wāw in يسمعون, or from الصيحة; ذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject); يوم الخروج: khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:43-43.t: ﴿إنا نحن نحيي ونميت وإلينا المصير﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿نا﴾: its noun; نحن: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), or a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause نحيي is the khabar (predicate) of إن, or the khabar of نحن, the [latter] clause then being the khabar of إن; إلينا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar; المصير: a postponed mubtadaʾ.

muyesser-irab:44-44.t: ﴿يوم تشقق الأرض عنهم سراعا ذلك حشر علينا يسير﴾: the adverb is a badal (substitute) from what precedes it; some disallowed this because of its multiplicity, and attached it to المصير; the clause تشقق is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the adverb's annexation to it; الأرض: fāʿil (agent); عنهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تشقق﴾; سراعًا: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in عنهم; ذلك: mubtadaʾ (subject); حشر: khabar (predicate); علينا: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يسير; and يسير is the khabar of ذلك.

muyesser-irab:45-45.t:
﴿نحن أعلم بما يقولون﴾: ﴿نحن﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أعلم﴾: khabar (predicate); ﴿بما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, i.e. "We know best that which they say"; or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿ما يقولون﴾ is genitive by the bāʾ, i.e. "their saying"; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعلم; the clause ﴿يقولون﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿وما أنت عليهم بجبار﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; ﴿ما﴾: the Ḥijāzī negative mā, which operates like ليس; ﴿أنت﴾: the noun of ما; ﴿عليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿جبار﴾; ﴿بجبار﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition, and ﴿جبار﴾ is the khabar of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative in position and genitive by the bāʾ in wording.
﴿فذكر بالقرآن من يخاف وعيد﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition); ذكر: an imperative verb; بالقرآن: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿ذكر﴾; من: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause يخاف is the ṣila, with no grammatical position. وعيد: the object of يخاف; the yāʾ of the first person was dropped in conformity with the [Muṣḥaf] script.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t: ﴿بل كذبوا بالحق لما جاءهم فهم في أمر مريج﴾: بل: a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and a conjunction of digression; كذبوا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); بالحق: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبوا﴾; لما: temporal (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya, "when"), or linking (rābiṭa); فهم: the fāʾ is a conjunction; هم: mubtadaʾ (subject); أمر: khabar (predicate); مريج: an adjective.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t: ﴿أفلم ينظروا إلى السماء فوقهم كيف بنيناها وزيناها وما لها من فروج﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī); the fāʾ conjoins to something omitted; لم: a particle of negation, of conversion [to past meaning] and of the jussive; ينظروا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); إلى السماء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينظروا﴾; كيف: an interrogative noun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as a ḥāl (circumstantial); بنيناها: a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is a badal (substitute) from السماء; the wāw is circumstantial (for the ḥāl); ما: negative; لها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); من: a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) preposition; فروج: genitive in wording, a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) in position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿والأرض مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; الأرض is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the position of ﴿إلى السماء﴾, which is the accusative as an object; the clause مددناها is a ḥāl (circumstantial); or ﴿الأرض﴾ is made accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "ومددنا الأرض" ("and We spread the earth"); ألقينا is conjoined to مددنا; فيها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ألقينا; رواسي: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. firmly-set, stable mountains.
﴿وأنبتنا فيها من كل زوج بهيج﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أنبتنا is also conjoined to what precedes; فيها: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أنبتنا; من كل زوج: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of an omitted object, the implied form being: "فأنبتنا فيها نباتًا كائنًا من كل زوج" ("and We caused to grow in it vegetation of every kind"); زوج: muḍāf ilayhi; بهيج: an adjective of زوج.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿تبصرة﴾: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) of the preceding verbs in His words ﴿بنيناها وزيناها﴾ and His words ﴿مددناها وألقينا فيها رواسي وأنبتنا فيها﴾, i.e. so that the actions mentioned and what they govern may be an insight; or: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied verb, because it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar), i.e. "He gave them insight"; or: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent), i.e. "giving insight"; or: a ḥāl from the object with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "possessing insight for whoever sees it".
﴿وذكرى﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿تبصرة﴾, accusative.
﴿لكل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تبصرة﴾.
﴿عبد﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿منيب﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of عبد.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t: ﴿ونزلنا من السماء ماء مباركا فأنبتنا به جنات وحب الحصيد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; نزلنا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); من السماء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نزلنا; ماء: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); مباركًا: an adjective; فأنبتنا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نزلنا; به: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أنبتنا; جنات: mafʿūl bihi; حب الحصيد is conjoined to جنات, and the qualified noun (mawṣūf) has been omitted.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
ق is not declined (muʿrab), because it is a letter of the alphabet. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have already mentioned its meaning. وَالْقُرْآنِ is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of the oath. الْمَجِيدِ is its naʿt (adjective). Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: «المجيد» means "the noble". As for the answer to the oath, there are four answers concerning it: al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: [it is] قَدْ عَلِمْنا ما تَنْقُصُ الْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ [Qāf: 4]. Abū Isḥāq said: the answer is omitted, i.e. "By the glorious Qur'an, you will surely be resurrected (لتبعثنّ)". And it was said:
rather, what is omitted is what the context of the speech indicates, because they said: "This Prophet is a strange thing"; they were astonished that a man from the sons of Adam should be sent to them, so the threat fell upon that, i.e. "By the glorious Qur'an, you will surely come to know the outcome of your denial on the Day of Resurrection", whereupon they said: أَإِذا مِتْنا. Abū Jaʿfar said: These are two answers. And whoever says:
"the meaning is: the matter has been decided, by Allah" — it does not need an answer, because the oath is placed in the middle, as you say: "I have spoken to you, by Allah, today." The fourth answer is that «ق» is a name for the mountain encompassing the earth; Wahb ibn Munabbih said that. The implied form would then be: "It is Qāf, by Allah", so on this view Qāf is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ).
Abū Jaʿfar said: The soundest of the answers is that the answer is omitted because [the context] indicates it, since إذا متنا is an answer, and «إذا» must necessarily be attached (mutaʿalliq) to a verb, i.e. "Shall we be resurrected when…". As for the answer being قد علمنا, that is an error, because «قد» is not among the answers of oaths. And if Qāf is a name for the mountain, then the proper course with it is to decline it (iʿrāb).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: بَلْ عَجِبُوا أَنْ جاءَهُمْ مُنْذِرٌ مِنْهُمْ, i.e. they did not deny you because they did not know you to be truthful; rather, they were astonished that he came to them with the message of the Lord of the Worlds. فَقالَ الْكافِرُونَ هذا شَيْءٌ عَجِيبٌ.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: أَإِذا مِتْنا, i.e. "Shall we be resurrected when we have died?" وَكُنَّا تُراباً ذلِكَ رَجْعٌ بَعِيدٌ: the meaning of بعيد according to al-Farrāʾ is "it will not happen". And that is well known in the language.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: قَدْ عَلِمْنا ما تَنْقُصُ الْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ, i.e. of their flesh and bodies. وَعِنْدَنا كِتابٌ حَفِيظٌ, in the sense of "preserving" (حافظ), because it does not wear away nor change.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِالْحَقِّ لَمَّا جاءَهُمْ, i.e. they did not deny you because of anything that had become apparent to them. فَهُمْ فِي أَمْرٍ مَرِيجٍ: it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: «مريج» means "objectionable"; and from him: "مريج: in error"; and from him: "مريج: discordant". Mujāhid and Qatāda said: "مريج: confused". Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Zayd said: "مريج: mixed up". Abū Jaʿfar said: These sayings, even though their wordings differ, are close in their meanings, because when a matter is discordant it is confused, objectionable and in error, since the truth is clear and evident.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: I.e. Have these polytheists, who denied the resurrection and rejected Our power to bring them back to life after decay, not looked at Our power to create the heaven, such that We made it a guarded roof? وَزَيَّنَّاها, i.e. with the stars. وَما لَها مِنْ فُرُوجٍ: [فروج] may be a plural, and may be a singular, i.e. "of any rifts and cracks".

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
وَالْأَرْضَ مَدَدْناها, i.e. "We spread it out". الأرض is accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and We spread out the earth". The nominative is permissible, except that the accusative is better, so that the verb is conjoined to a verb. وَأَلْقَيْنا فِيها رَواسِيَ, i.e. mountains that are anchored (رست) in the earth, i.e. are firm. وَأَنْبَتْنا فِيها مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ, i.e. kind. Ibn ʿAbbās said:
بَهِيجٍ means "beautiful".

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
تَبْصِرَةً is a maṣdar (verbal noun) and a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. "We did that in order to make you see the power of Allah, glory be to Him". وَذِكْرى, i.e. and so that you may remember the greatness of Allah and His authority, and so know that He is able to give life to the dead and to do whatever He wills.
لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُنِيبٍ, i.e. one returning to faith and to obedience to Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: وَنَزَّلْنا مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً مُبارَكاً, which is the rain. فَأَنْبَتْنا بِهِ جَنَّاتٍ وَحَبَّ الْحَصِيدِ: al-Farrāʾ claimed that a thing has been annexed to itself, because in his view the grain (الحب) is the harvested (الحصيد). Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān relate from the Basrans, among them Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, that annexing a thing to itself is impossible; rather, the implied form is "the grain of the harvested plant" (حبّ النبت الحصيد).

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: وَالنَّخْلَ باسِقاتٍ, i.e. "and We caused the palm trees to grow tall". It is an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial; ḥāl muqaddara): «باسقات» is [accusative] as a ḥāl. لَها طَلْعٌ نَضِيدٌ: you make طلع nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), even though it is indefinite, because of the benefit [of information] in it.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
رِزْقاً لِلْعِبادِ: Abū Isḥāq said: رزقا is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and it may be a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose).
وَأَحْيَيْنا بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتاً, i.e. barren, with no crops or vegetation in it. كَذلِكَ الْخُرُوجُ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), i.e. your coming out of your graves is like this: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sends water and by it causes people to grow as crops grow. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "just as We created these things, We shall resurrect you".

nahhas-irab:12-14.t:
كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ, i.e. before these polytheists who denied Muḥammad ﷺ, the people of Nūḥ denied; the tāʾ is for the feminine of the collective. وَأَصْحابُ الرَّسِّ وَثَمُودُ وَعادٌ وَفِرْعَوْنُ وَإِخْوانُ لُوطٍ (13). وَأَصْحابُ الْأَيْكَةِ: Mujāhid said: الرّسّ is a well. Qatāda said: الأيكة is the dense, intertwined trees. وَقَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ: all of it is conjunction (ʿaṭf). Abū Mijlaz said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās asked Kaʿb about Tubbaʿ, and he said: He was a righteous man; he took some young men from the rabbis and made them his intimates, and he became Muslim, and his people objected to that from him. And in the ḥadīth of Sahl ibn Saʿd from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: «Do not curse Tubbaʿ, for he had become Muslim.» كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ: the implied form according to Sībawayh is "all of them" (كلّهم), then [the pronoun] was omitted because كلّ indicates it. All the grammarians permitted "كلّ منطلق" in the sense of "all of them are departing". Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd permit dropping the nunation (tanwīn), saying "كلّ منطلق" in the sense of "all of them", treating it as a ghāya (a word cut off from its annexed term) like قبل and بعد. ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: This is the speech of someone who does not know why قبل and بعد are made indeclinable (mabnī), and [what is] analogous to this among the words, because the grammarians have restricted [this] to the adverbs (ẓurūf) on account of the cause that is in them and not in other [words]. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a clear and correct statement according to the people of Arabic.
The yāʾ was dropped from وَعِيدِ because it is the end of a verse, so that the verses do not differ. As for the one who retains it in continuous reading (al-idrāj) and drops it in pause, his argument is that the pause is a place of dropping; the proof of that is that you say لم يمض, and when you continue [the speech] you give the ḍād a kasra and nothing else. The meaning of فَحَقَّ وَعِيدِ is: so the threat from Allah, Majestic and Mighty, of punishment in the Hereafter and of retribution became binding upon the disbelievers.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
أَفَعَيِينا بِالْخَلْقِ الْأَوَّلِ: one says "عيينا بالأمر" and "عييّ به" when one could not find one's way in it and did not master it. When you say عيينا, assimilation (idghām) is not permitted, because the second letter is vowelless, so if you assimilated it into the first two vowelless letters would meet. As for the meaning, it was said to those who denied the resurrection and said (ذلك رجع بعيد): "Were We wearied by the initial creation, so that We should be wearied by bringing you back to life after decay?" ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās:
أفعيينا بالخلق الأول — he said: He is saying, "We were not wearied by it." Abū Jaʿfar said: And thus the interrogative that contains the meaning of affirmation (taqrīr) and rebuke takes on the meaning of negation, i.e. He was not wearied by the first creation. بَلْ هُمْ فِي لَبْسٍ مِنْ خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ, i.e. about the resurrection.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ وَنَعْلَمُ ما تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ: the pronoun in به refers back to «ما». Al-Farrāʾ permitted that it refer to الإنسان, i.e. "and He knows what his soul whispers to him". وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ: Ibn ʿAbbās said: الوريد is the vein of the neck. The grammarians have two implied readings of it: al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: "And We are nearer to him in power than the jugular vein". Someone else said: i.e. "And We are nearer to him in knowledge of what his soul whispers to him than the jugular vein".

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: And He did not say قعيدان (two seated ones); there are several answers to this. The school of Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī is that the meaning is "on the right a seated one and on the left a seated one", and then [one of them] was omitted. The school of al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ is that «قعيد» is a singular that stands for two and for more than two, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا [Ghāfir: 67]. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: the implied form in قَعِيدٌ is that it is intended to be placed earlier, i.e. "on the right a seated one", and then "and on the left" is conjoined to it. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is clear and good, and similar to it is وَاللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُرْضُوهُ [al-Tawba: 62]. A fourth view is that قعيد is in the sense of a group, as the Arabs use the faʿīl pattern; He, Majestic and Mighty, said: وَالْمَلائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ [al-Taḥrīm: 4].

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: ما يَلْفِظُ مِنْ قَوْلٍ: the pronoun in it refers back to الإنسان, i.e. man does not utter any word, speaking it, except that at [the moment] he utters it there is رَقِيبٌ, i.e. a guardian who records it against him. عَتِيدٌ means "prepared" (معدّ). This is among the uses of the faʿīl pattern: it can have the sense of a plural, the sense of mufʿal, the sense of mafʿūl, like قتيل (killed), and the sense of fāʿil, like قدير in the sense of قادر (able).

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: وَجاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ, i.e. its intensity and its overpowering of a person's understanding, so that he becomes like one drunk from drink or from sleep. بِالْحَقِّ, i.e. with the matter of the Hereafter, which is true, until he sees it clearly with his own eyes. Another view is that الحقّ is death, i.e. "and the stupor of death came with the reality of death". It is soundly reported from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read «وجاءت سكرة الحقّ بالموت», and likewise from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, Allah's mercy be upon him. He said: This is a reading by way of explanation (tafsīr). There are two views on its meaning: الحقّ may be Allah, Majestic and Mighty, i.e. "and the stupor [from] Allah came with death"; the other view is that of al-Farrāʾ: the stupor is itself the truth, "and the stupor, the truth, came", a thing annexed to itself. ذلِكَ ما كُنْتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيدُ, i.e. that stupor is what you used to flee from. As for the masculine [ذلك], it is in the sense of "that drunkenness" (ذلك السّكر).

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: I.e. what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, threatened the disbelievers and the people of sins with: the Fire.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: It is construed according to the meaning; had it been according to the wording, it would have been «وجاء كلّ نفس معه». The implied form is «ومعها»; the wāw was omitted because of the returning pronoun, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
لَقَدْ كُنْتَ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هذا: the people of knowledge differed as to whom this address is directed, and they have three views on it. Zayd ibn Aslam and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān said that this address is to the Prophet ﷺ. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb related from Yaʿqūb from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said: I said to Zayd ibn Aslam, "And is this address to the Prophet ﷺ?" He said: "What do you find objectionable in this, when Allah, glory be to Him, has said: أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيماً فَآوى وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدى [al-Ḍuḥā: 6, 7]?" He said: So this is one view. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: لَقَدْ كُنْتَ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هذا — he said: This is an address to the disbelievers. Mujāhid said the same. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: an address to the polytheists. Ṣāliḥ ibn Kaysān, after objecting to what Zayd ibn Aslam said, said: "He is not knowledgeable in the speech of the Arabs, nor does he have [that]; rather, this is an address to the disbelievers."
These are two views. The third view is what al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās said:
This is an address to the righteous and the wicked; and it is the view of Qatāda. Abū Jaʿfar said: As for the view of Zayd ibn Aslam, its interpretation is that in his view the speech is complete at His saying, Majestic and Mighty: وَجاءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَعَها سائِقٌ وَشَهِيدٌ (21); then He began anew: "O Muḥammad, you were heedless of this religion and of what was revealed to you, before you were sent, when you were in the Jāhiliyya". فَكَشَفْنا عَنْكَ غِطاءَكَ, i.e. "so We made you see". فَبَصَرُكَ الْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ, i.e. "so your knowledge is penetrating".
Sight (البصر) here is in the sense of knowledge. The most fitting thing said about the verse is that it is general, for the righteous and the wicked; what indicates that is وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ وَنَعْلَمُ ما تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ, for this is general for all people, righteous and wicked. Thus it is known that the meaning of وَجاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ is "and the stupor of death came to you, O man"; then the address continues on this [basis] in لَقَدْ كُنْتَ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هذا, i.e. "you were, O man, heedless of what you have now seen with your eyes". If he was a doer of good, he regrets that he did not do more; and if he was an evildoer, he regrets that he did not desist. This is when the covering has been removed from both of them, so "your sight today is penetrating" for what you have seen. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "فبصرك: the tongue of the balance."
It was said: some scholars interpreted this as a likeness for justice, i.e. "you are the one of Allah's creatures, Majestic and Mighty, who knows best your own deeds, so your sight of them is like the tongue of the balance by which excess and deficiency are known".

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: وَقالَ قَرِينُهُ: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd said: «قرينه» is his driver who has been put in charge of him. هذا ما لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ: he said: this is what he took and brought. هذا is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); ما is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and عَتِيدٌ is a second khabar. It may be nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ; it may be a badal (substitute) from «ما»; and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of ما, if you make «ما» indefinite. The accusative is permissible outside the Qur'an, like وَهذا بَعْلِي شَيْخاً [Hūd: 72].

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
The grammarians differed concerning His saying ألقيا. Some said: it is an address to the companion (القرين), i.e. it is said to the companion: ألقيا. This is the view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ, and he claimed that the Arabs address one person with the address for two, saying "O man, stand (قوما)!", and he recited [in the ṭawīl metre]:
432-
خليليّ مرّا بي على أمّ جندب ... لنقضي حاجات الفؤاد المعذّب
(My two friends, pass with me by Umm Jundab, that we may fulfil the needs of the tormented heart.)
 He was addressing only one person, and he inferred that from his saying [in the ṭawīl metre]: 433-
ألم تر أنّي كلما جئت طارقا ... وجدت بها طيبا وإن لم تطيّب
(Have you not seen that whenever I came by night, I found fragrance in her, even though she was not perfumed?)
Others said: «قرين» is used for a group, for one and for two, like وَالْمَلائِكَةُ بَعْدَ ذلِكَ ظَهِيرٌ [al-Taḥrīm: 4]. Abū Jaʿfar said: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān told us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd from Bakr ibn Muḥammad al-Māzinī, who said: The Arabs say to one person قوما on one condition: when they mean repetition of the verb, i.e. "stand, stand" (قم قم); so they brought the alif to indicate this meaning, and likewise «ألقيا». Another view: it is an address to two. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd said: [it is addressed to] the driver and the guardian together. Mujāhid and ʿIkrima said:
العنيد is the one who shuns the truth and who stubbornly opposes Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: عنيد is in the sense of معاند (stubborn opponent), like ضجيع (bedfellow) and جليس (sitting companion).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ, i.e. of what is obligatory upon him, of zakāt and other things; and الخير is wealth. ومُعْتَدٍ: [aggressing] against people with his tongue and his hand. Qatāda said: مُرِيبٍ means "doubting".

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: الَّذِي جَعَلَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلهاً آخَرَ: «الذي» may be in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from كلّ, or in the sense of "I mean" (أعني); and it may be nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar (predicate) is فَأَلْقِياهُ فِي الْعَذابِ الشَّدِيدِ.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: قالَ قَرِينُهُ رَبَّنا ما أَطْغَيْتُهُ, i.e. "I did not make him a transgressor (طاغيا)", i.e. one who oversteps into disbelief. وَلكِنْ كانَ فِي ضَلالٍ بَعِيدٍ, i.e. on a path deviating from the truth.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: قالَ لا تَخْتَصِمُوا لَدَيَّ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa said from Ibn ʿAbbās: They offered excuses without any [valid] excuse, so He invalidated their argument against them. وَقَدْ قَدَّمْتُ إِلَيْكُمْ بِالْوَعِيدِ, i.e. with the threat in which there is no injustice and which will not be broken; so do not dispute before Me.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: ما يُبَدَّلُ الْقَوْلُ لَدَيَّ: Mujāhid said: i.e. "I have decreed what I decree". وَما أَنَا بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ, i.e. "I do not seize anyone for another's crime".

nahhas-irab:30-30.t:
يَوْمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ امْتَلَأْتِ: the governing word (ʿāmil) in يوم is ظلام. وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِنْ مَزِيدٍ: there are two views on its meaning. One of them is that the meaning is "there is no more" (ما في مزيد), and the holder of this view argues from His saying, Majestic and Mighty:
لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ [al-Sajda: 13; Ṣād: 85]. This is the view of ʿIkrima, and analogous to it is the ḥadīth when it was said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Will you not stay in one of your houses?" and he said: «And has ʿAqīl left us any house?», i.e. he did not leave us a house, for he sold it at the time of the Hijra. So this is one view. The other view is فهل من مزيد as a request for more. This is the view of Anas ibn Mālik, and what indicates it is the sound ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: «Jahannam will keep saying "Is there any more?", and the Lord of the Worlds, glory be to Him and exalted, will place His foot in it, and it will say: "Enough, enough (قط قط)."» Abū Jaʿfar said: This ḥadīth has a sound chain of transmission (isnād), and it indicates the opposite of the first view. And Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows best.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: I.e. near for the God-fearing, i.e. those who guard themselves against disobeying Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: هذا ما تُوعَدُونَ, i.e. this which We have described for the God-fearing is what you are promised. لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ: Ibn Zayd said: for every one who repents, returning to Allah in obedience to Him. And from Ibn ʿAbbās: أَوَّابٍ means one who glorifies [Allah]; and from him: حَفِيظٍ, one who remembered his sins until he repented of them. Qatāda said: «حفيظ» means one who preserves what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, entrusted him with; and the meaning of this is that he guarded his limbs from disobeying Allah the Exalted.

nahhas-irab:33-34.t: مَنْ خَشِيَ الرَّحْمنَ بِالْغَيْبِ is in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) from «كلّ», and it may be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with خَشِيَ in the position of the jussive as the condition (sharṭ). The implied form is: خَشِيَ الرَّحْمنَ بِالْغَيْبِ وَجاءَ بِقَلْبٍ مُنِيبٍ, so it will be said to them: ادْخُلُوها — according to the meaning of من, while what precedes it is according to its wording. مُنِيبٍ: one who repents, returning to Allah, Majestic and Mighty. ذلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُلُودِ, i.e. that which We have described for the God-fearing is a day from which they will never depart.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: لَهُمْ ما يَشاؤُنَ فِيها, i.e. they will have whatever they want, and more by way of honour. Anas ibn Mālik explained the meaning of وَلَدَيْنا مَزِيدٌ — and since [such a thing] cannot be taken by personal suggestion and can only be taken from the Prophet, upon him be peace — concerning وَلَدَيْنا مَزِيدٌ he said: He said: «The Lord of the Worlds will manifest Himself to them and say: By My might, I shall manifest Myself to you so that you look at Me. And He will say: Welcome to My servants, My neighbours, My visitors and My delegation; look at Me.» That is the utmost of giving and the bounty of the "more".

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ, i.e. before the polytheists of Quraysh who denied you. هُمْ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ بَطْشاً: those destroyed were stronger than those who denied you. [بطشا] is accusative as clarification (bayān, i.e. tamyīz). فَنَقَّبُوا فِي الْبِلادِ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa said from Ibn ʿAbbās: فَنَقَّبُوا فِي الْبِلادِ means "they left their traces", and its literal meaning in the language is "they roamed about and penetrated deep".
هَلْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ: al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. "Did they have any escape from death?", and كان was omitted because [the context] indicates it. The reading of Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar فَنَقَّبُوا is anomalous (shādhdh), departing from the majority, and it is by way of threat. [Translator's note: the variant is printed here with the same spelling as the standard reading; the source does not show how Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar's variant differs in vowelling; the remark "by way of threat" suggests an imperative.]

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَذِكْرى, i.e. in Our destruction of the generations whom We destroyed and whose story We have related.
لَذِكْرى: by which one who has a heart with which he understands is reminded. أَوْ أَلْقَى السَّمْعَ, i.e. listened attentively. وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ: understanding, not heedless; and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:38-38.t:
The hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) was kept in ستة because it is a number for a masculine [noun], and you distinguish between it and the feminine. The meaning of يوم is:
a period of time; that is why it is mentioned before the creation of daytime. وَما مَسَّنا مِنْ لُغُوبٍ: from لغب يلغب and يلغب, when one becomes tired.

nahhas-irab:39-40.t:
فَاصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ — for I am lying in wait for them — وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ. The people of tafsīr said: He means by it the Jews, because they said "He rested on the Sabbath day". He, Majestic and Mighty, said: "So be patient over what they say, for I am lying in wait for them", وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ — the people of tafsīr took it in the sense of prayer, and likewise وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ. Ibn Zayd said: [it is] the ʿatama (night prayer). Mujāhid said: the whole night. It was said: He means the Maghrib and the later ʿIshāʾ. He said:
This is more fitting, because of the generality of "the night" in the apparent sense of the verse. وَأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ: there are two views on it. Ibn Zayd said:
the supererogatory prayers (nawāfil). He said: This is a clear view, because the verse is general, so it is taken as general unless some proof comes [to restrict it]; except that the argument of the majority has come [to the effect] that the meaning of وَأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ is two rakʿas after Maghrib. That was said by ʿUmar, ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with them, and among the Successors by al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, al-Shaʿbī, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Some of the ḥadīth scholars trace the ḥadīth of ʿAlī back to the Prophet ﷺ: (وإدبار السجود) — he said: «two rakʿas after Maghrib». Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read وَأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ with a fatḥa on the hamza, making it the plural of دبر; and whoever says إدبار makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun) of أدبر. They all agreed on the kasra in وَإِدْبارَ النُّجُومِ [al-Ṭūr: 49]. Abū ʿUbayd mentioned that prostration has no "going back" (إدبار). This is among the things held against him, because the meaning of وأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ is "what comes after it and what follows it", so this applies to prostration, and the stars and man are the same [in this respect]. The eminent ḥadīth scholars have related the explanation of وَأَدْبارَ السُّجُودِ and وَإِدْبارَ النُّجُومِ, and we do not know of any of them who distinguished between the two.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read يَوْمَ يُنادِ الْمُنادِ مِنْ مَكانٍ قَرِيبٍ without a yāʾ, both in continuous reading and in pause; and this is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, following the script. Some opposed him and said: there is no change of the script in this, because the yāʾ is the final radical (lām al-fiʿl) of the verb, so it is known that its due is to remain. Sībawayh said: what is good in the like of this is retaining the yāʾ in pause and in continuous reading. He said: and it is permissible to drop it in pause. Abū Jaʿfar said: That is because you say مناد, then you add the alif and lām, and you do not change the noun from its state. As for the meaning of وَاسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنادِ الْمُنادِ مِنْ مَكانٍ قَرِيبٍ (41),
it was said concerning it: i.e. "[listen for] the time of the day". Kaʿb said: The caller is an angel who calls from a near place, from the Rock of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), with a loud voice: "O decayed bones and severed joints, gather together for the final judgement!"

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ الصَّيْحَةَ بِالْحَقِّ, i.e. with the gathering for the reckoning. ذلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُرُوجِ: from their graves.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي وَنُمِيتُ: the object is omitted, i.e. "We give life to the dead and cause the living to die". وَإِلَيْنَا الْمَصِيرُ, i.e. the return.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ الْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِراعاً: the governing word (ʿāmil) in «يوم» is المصير, i.e. "and to Us is their return on the day [the earth] splits apart (تتشقّق)". In تَشَقَّقُ the tāʾ was assimilated into the shīn; and whoever says تشقّق dropped the tāʾ. سِراعاً is [accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it was said: from the hāʾ and the mīm [of عنهم]; and it was said: a ḥāl from the hāʾ and the mīm is not permissible, because there is no governing word over it; rather, the implied form is "so they come out hastening" (فيخرجون سراعا). ذلِكَ حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنا يَسِيرٌ, i.e. easy.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِما يَقُولُونَ وَما أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخافُ وَعِيدِ (45). نَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِما يَقُولُونَ, i.e. of the fabrication and the denial of the resurrection. وَما أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبَّارٍ, i.e. "one given authority [over them]". Al-Farrāʾ said: جبّار has been put in the place of سلطان (one with authority). Whoever says that بجبّار means "you do not compel them (تجبرهم) to what you want" is mistaken, because the faʿʿāl pattern is not formed from afʿala; and even though al-Farrāʾ related that one says درّاك from أدرك, this is anomalous and unknown. He also related "جبرت الرجل" (I compelled the man), and this is among the anomalies, even though some of the jurists are fond of جبرت. فَذَكِّرْ بِالْقُرْآنِ مَنْ يَخافُ وَعِيدِ, i.e. My threat to whoever disobeys Me and opposes My command.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ}: It is permissible that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الجنة». It was not made feminine either because it has the sense of «البستان» (the garden), or because the form «فعيل» is not made feminine, since it is of the pattern of verbal nouns; al-Zamakhsharī said this, but the Shaykh did not concede it. What was said earlier on His saying {إِنَّ رَحْمَتَ الله قَرِيبٌ} [الأعراف: 56] spares you this. It is also permissible that it be accusative as an adverbial of place (ẓarf), that is, "a place not far"; and it is permissible that it be a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), that is, «إزلافاً غير بعيد» ("a bringing near that is not far"). This is the apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's wording, for he said: «or something not far».

semin-durr:32-32.t: His saying: {هذا مَا تُوعَدُونَ}: Two views are permissible for this clause. The first: that it is parenthetical between the badal (substitute) and the one substituted for, because «لكل أَوَّابٍ» is a badal from «للمتقين» with repetition of the governing element. The second: that it is governed by an implied saying, and that saying is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is, "it being said to them". It was already mentioned in Sūrat Ṣād that «تُوعَدون» was read with the tāʾ and with the yāʾ. The Shaykh ascribed the reading with the yāʾ (with two dots below) here to Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr, but it is in fact from Ibn Kathīr alone.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {مَّنْ خَشِيَ}: It is permissible that it be genitive in position, as a badal (substitute) or a bayān (explicative apposition) of «كل». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is permissible that it be a badal after a badal, following «كل»." He means that it is a badal from «كل» after «لكل» was made a badal from «للمتقين»; and he did not make it a further badal of «للمتقين» itself, because the badal is not repeated when the one substituted for is one. It is also permissible that it be a badal for the noun qualified by «أوّاب» and «حفيظ», as al-Zamakhsharī said; he means that the original is «لكل شخصٍ أوّابٍ» ("for every person who is oft-returning"), so «مَنْ خَشِي» would be a badal from the implied «شخص». He said: "It cannot be in the status of «أوّاب» and «حفيظ» (that is, an adjective), because «مَنْ» is not used as an adjective, and among the relative nouns only «الذي» is used as a qualifier." By his saying "in the status of «أوّاب»" he means that «مَنْ» would be made an adjective, and this, as he said, is not permissible. However, the Shaykh took exception to his restriction and said: "Rather, it is qualified by relatives other than «الذي», such as their qualifying with what contains the relative «أل», as in «الضارب» and «المضروب», and such as their qualifying with the two Ṭayyiʾ forms «ذو» and «ذات», as in their saying: «بالفضل ذو فَضَّلكم اللَّهُ به والكرامةِ ذاتُ أكرمكم اللَّهُ بَهْ»."
Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed «مَنْ خَشِي» to be a naʿt (adjective) of what preceded; this is rejected by what has been said. It is also permissible that «مَنْ خَشِي» be nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or accusative by an omitted verb, both by way of qaṭʿ (cutting off), which signals praise; and that it be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is an implied saying that governs His words «ادْخُلوها», that is: "those who feared the Most Merciful, it will be said to them: Enter it." It was first construed according to the wording and in the second place according to the meaning. It was also said that «مَنْ خَشي» is a vocative whose particle of address has been omitted, that is, "O you who feared, enter it," in accordance with the two earlier constructions; and that it be conditional, its apodosis (jawāb) omitted, namely that saying, but with a «فاء» returned with it, that is, «فيقال لهم» ("then it will be said to them"). As for «بالغيب», it is a ḥāl, that is, "unseen by Him"; it may be a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent), from the object, or from both. It was also said that the «باء» is causal, that is, "fear because of the unseen punishment of His with which He threatened"; and it is permissible that it be an adjective of the maṣdar of «خشي», that is, "he feared Him with a fear coupled with the unseen".

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {بِسَلاَمٍ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «ادْخلوها», that is, "safe from calamities", in which case it is a concurrent ḥāl; or "greeted with peace upon you", in which case it is an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), like His saying {فادخلوها خَالِدِينَ} [الزمر: 73]; so it was said. There is room for objection in this, for nothing prevents the angels' greeting of them from coinciding with the time of entering, unlike {فادخلوها خَالِدِينَ} [الزمر: 73], since eternity cannot be conceived except after entering.
His saying: {ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ الخلود}: Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "That is, the time of that is the Day of Eternity," as if he made «ذلك» point to the favour of Allah upon them just mentioned. There is no need for this; rather «ذلك» points to the time that comes after it, as in your saying «هذا زيدٌ» ("this is Zayd").
His saying: {فِيهَا}: It is permissible that it be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَشاؤُون», and it is permissible that it be a ḥāl from the relative noun or from its returning pronoun; the first is preferable.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا}: «كم» is accusative by what follows it. It was put first either because it is interrogative, or because the declarative «كم» is treated like the interrogative in taking the front position. «مِنْ قَرْن» is a tamyīz (specification), and «هم أشدُّ» is an adjective, either of «كم» or of «قرن».
His saying: {فَنَقَّبُواْ}: The «فاء» is a conjunction according to the sense, as if it had been said: "their might was great, so they searched about". The pronoun in «نَقَّبوا» is either for the earlier generations, which is the apparent sense, or for Quraysh. What supports this is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Yaʿmar, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Naṣr ibn Sayyār, Abū Ḥaywa and al-Aṣmaʿī on the authority of Abū ʿAmr, «فَنَقِّبوا» with kasra on the «قاف», as a command to them to do so. «التنقيب» is searching and investigating, and its meaning is roaming through the lands. Al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza said:
4097 - نَقَّبوا في البلاد مِنْ حَذَرِ الموْ ... تِ وجالُوا في الأرض كلَّ مجَالِ
(They roamed the lands in fear of death, and ranged over the earth in every direction.)
And Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4098 - وقد نَقَّبْتُ في الآفاقِ حتى ... رَضِيْتُ مِن الغنيمة بالإِياب
(I have roamed the horizons until I was content, in place of booty, with returning.)
Ibn ʿAbbās and Abū ʿAmr also read, in one transmission, «نَقَبوا» with fatḥa on the «قاف», light (without shadda); its meaning is as above. It was also read «نَقِبوا» with kasra, light, that is, their feet and the feet of their camels became weary and bled, the first term of the genitive construct (muḍāf) having been omitted, and that is because of their great roaming.
His saying: {هَلْ مِن مَّحِيصٍ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is implied, its implied form being: "Is there for whoever follows their path," or "Is there for them any escape?" This clause may or may not be taken as being governed by an implied saying.

semin-durr:37-37.t: His saying: {أَوْ أَلْقَى}: The majority read «أَلْقى» in the active voice. Al-Sulamī, Ṭalḥa, al-Suddī and Abū al-Barhasam read «أُلْقِي» in the passive, with «السَّمعُ» made nominative by it. This reading was attributed to ʿĀṣim on the authority of al-Suddī, whom he detested for it and said: "Does He not say «يُلْقُوْن السَّمْعَ»?"

semin-durr:38-38.t: His saying: {وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِن لُّغُوبٍ}: It is permissible that it be a ḥāl (circumstantial), and that it be resumptive. The majority read «اللُّغوب» with ḍamma on the «لام»; ʿAlī, Ṭalḥa, al-Sulamī and Yaʿqūb read it with fatḥa. They are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) of the same meaning. This should be added to what Sībawayh reported of the maṣdars that come on this pattern, which are five, and to what al-Kisāʾī added, namely «الوَزُوع», making them seven. I have treated this thoroughly in al-Baqara at His saying {وَقُودُهَا} [الآية: 24].

semin-durr:40-40.t:
His saying: {وَأَدْبَارَ}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Ḥamza read «إِدْبار» with kasra on the hamza, as a maṣdar (verbal noun) standing in the place of an adverbial of time, as in their saying «آتيك خُفوقَ النجمِ وخلافة الحجَّاج» ("I will come to you at the setting of the star and at the caliphate of al-Ḥajjāj"). The meaning is: "at the time of the end of the prayer", that is, its completion and fulfilment. The rest read it with fatḥa, as the plural of «دُبُر», which is the end of the prayer and what follows it; from this is the saying of Aws:
4099 - على دُبُرِ الشهرِ الحَرامِ فأَرْضُنا ... وما حولَها جَدْبٌ سِنونَ تَلْمَعُ
(At the close of the sacred month, our land and what is around it is barren, years of drought glittering.)
They did not differ on {وَإِدْبَارَ النجوم} [الطور: 49].

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {واستمع}: It is listening in its usual sense. It was also said that it means waiting, which is far-fetched. On the first view it is permissible that the object be omitted, that is, "listen for the call of the caller", or "the call of the disbeliever with woe and perdition"; on this «يومَ ينادي» is an adverbial of time for «استمع», that is, "listen for that on a day...".
It was also said: "listen to what I say to you." On this «يومَ يُنادي» is accusative by an implied «يَخْرجون» ("they will come out"), indicated by His saying {ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ الخروج} [ق: 42]; and on the second view (waiting) «يومَ ينادي» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), that is, "await that day".
Ibn Kathīr paused on «يُنادي» with the yāʾ, while the others paused without it. The reason for retaining it is that nothing requires its omission; the reason for omitting it in pausing is to follow the written form, and pausing is a place for lightening. As for «المنادي», Ibn Kathīr also retained its yāʾ both in continuous reading and in pausing; Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr retained it in continuous reading and omitted it in pausing; and the rest of the Seven omitted it in both. Whoever retained it did so because it is the original form; whoever omitted it did so to follow the written form; and whoever restricted the omission to pausing did so because pausing is a place of rest and a place of change.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ}: a badal (substitute) from «يومَ ينادي». «بالحق» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الصيحة», that is, "coupled with the truth", or from the fāʿil (agent), that is, "they hear, coupled with a true hearing".
His saying: {ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ الخروج}: It is permissible that the implied sense be "that time", that is, the time of the call and the hearing is the Day of Coming Out. It is also permissible that «ذلك» point to the call, in which case latitude has been taken with the adverbial so that it is predicated of the maṣdar (verbal noun); or a muḍāf (annexed noun) is implied before that call and hearing: "the call of the Day of Coming Out and its hearing".

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ}: «يوم» may be a badal (substitute) from the «يوم» before it. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is a badal from the first «يوم»." There is room for objection in this, because the badal would be repeated while the one substituted for is one; and it has already been mentioned that al-Zamakhsharī forbade it. It is also permissible that the day be an adverbial for «المصير» (the return). It was also said: an adverbial for the coming out. It was also said: accusative by an implied «يَخْرُجون». The disagreement about «يَشَّقَّقُ» was mentioned in al-Furqān. Zayd read «تَتَشَقَّق» with the doubling undone.
His saying: {سِرَاعاً}: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عنهم», and the operator on it is «تَشَقَّقُ». It was also said that its operator is the one operating on the implied «يوم تَشَقَّقُ», that is, «يَخْرُجون سِراعاً يوم تَشَقَّقُ» ("they will come out hastening on the day it splits open").
His saying: {عَلَيْنَا}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «يَسير», so the object of the adjective separates between it and what it qualifies, and this does no harm. It is also permissible that it be attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from it, because originally it may be an adjective. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The fronting is for restriction, that is, that is not easy except for Allah alone." The disagreement about the yāʾ of «وعيد», retained or omitted, was mentioned earlier.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {والقرآن}: an oath. There are several views about its answer. The first: that it is His saying {قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ الأرض}. The second: {مَا يُبَدَّلُ القول}. The third: {مَّا يَلْفِظُ مِن قَوْلٍ}. The fourth: {إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لذكرى}. The fifth: {بَلْ عجبوا}, which is a Kufan view; they said: because it is equivalent to «قد عَجِبوا». The sixth: that it is omitted; al-Zajjāj, al-Akhfash and al-Mubarrad supplied «لَتُبْعَثُنَّ» ("you will surely be resurrected"). ʿĪsā read «ق» with fatḥa, al-Ḥasan and Ibn Abī Isḥāq with kasra, and Hārūn and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ with ḍamma. The justification of all that has already passed: the fatḥa allows that it is indeclinable on fatḥa for lightness, or accusative by an implied verb and a diptote, or genitive by an implied oath particle, also a diptote. The ḍamma is on the view that it is a mubtadaʾ or a khabar, also a diptote.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {أَإِذَا مِتْنَا}: the majority read it with the interrogative; Ibn ʿĀmir in one transmission, Abū Jaʿfar, al-Aʿmash and al-Aʿraj read it with one hamza, which allows the interrogative, as with the majority, the particle being omitted because it is indicated, and also allows a statement of fact. The operator of the adverbial in the majority reading is implied, that is: "Shall we be resurrected, or shall we return, when we have died?" The apodosis of «إذا» in the reading as a statement is omitted, that is: "we shall return." It is also said that it is His saying «ذلك رَجْعٌ» with the fāʾ omitted, which is the view of some; the majority permit this only in poetry. al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is possible that «الرَّجْعُ», meaning «المَرْجوع», is the answer, and is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, expressing the improbability of their denial of what they were warned of regarding the resurrection. Pausing at what precedes it is good on this interpretation." If you ask: what then governs the adverbial if «الرَّجْعُ» means «المَرْجوع»? I say: what is indicated by the warner of the thing warned of, namely the resurrection." The Shaykh attacked him for understanding it so.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {بَلْ كَذَّبُواْ}: this is a second iḍrāb (turning from one statement to another). al-Zamakhsharī said: "An iḍrāb that follows the previous iḍrāb, to indicate that they came with something more shocking than their wonder, namely denying the truth." The Shaykh said: "It is as if this second iḍrāb were a substitute of retraction (badal badāʾ) for the first." I say: to apply such a term in the Book of Allah is not permissible at all. It is also said: before this verse there is a sentence turned away from, its implied form being: "They did not look well; rather they denied." What al-Zamakhsharī said is better.
The majority read «لَمَّا» with doubling, and it is either a particle of necessity for necessity, or an adverbial meaning "when", as you know. al-Jaḥdarī read it with kasra on the lām and the mīm light, on the basis that it is the lām of the genitive entering the maṣdar «ما», parallel to their saying «كتبْتُه لخمسٍ خَلَوْن» ("I wrote it on the fifth, the days having passed"), that is, at it.
His saying: {مَّرِيجٍ}: that is, confused. Abū Wāqid said:
4089 - مَرِجَ الدِّيْنُ فأَعْدَدْتُ له ... مُشْرِفَ الأَقْطارِ مَحْبوكَ الكَتَدْ
(Religion fell into disorder, so I prepared for it a tall-framed horse, with a well-knit withers.)
Another said:
4090 - فجالَتْ والتمسْتُ به حَشاها ... فَخَرَّ كأنَّه خُوْطٌ مَرِيْجُ
(She wheeled, and I sought her flank with it; he fell like a restless shoot.)
Its origin is from movement and agitation / and from it: «مَرَجَ الخاتمُ في إصبعِه» ("the ring was loose on his finger").

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {فَوْقَهُمْ}: a ḥāl from «السماء», and it is an emphatic one. And «كيف» is accusative by what follows it [source: «بعجها»] and it suspends the "looking" before it. [Translator's note: the source reads «بعجها»; this appears to be a misprint for «بعدها» ("after it"), and the translation follows that sense.]

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {تَبْصِرَةً}: the majority put it in the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, that is: "to give insight to people like them and as a reminder from Us to them." It is also said: both are accusative by a verb of their own wording, implied, that is: "Give them insight, an insight, and remind them, a reminder." It is also said: two ḥāls, that is: "given insight, reminded". It is also said: a ḥāl from the object, that is: "possessing insight and reminder for whoever sees it." Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it in the nominative. He read «وذِكْرٌ», that is: "it is an insight and a reminder." And «لكلِّ» is either an adjective or attached to the maṣdar itself.

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {وَحَبَّ الحصيد}: it may be a case of omitting the described noun because it is known, the implied form being: «وحَبَّ الزَرْعِ الحصيدِ» ("the grain of the harvested crop"), like «مسجد الجامع» and similar. This is the school of the Basrans, so that the annexation of a thing to itself is not necessary. It may also be a case of annexing the described noun to its adjective, because the original is «والحَبَّ الحصيدَ», that is, the harvested.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {والنخل}: accusative, conjoined to the object of «أَنْبَتْنا», that is: "and We caused the palm trees to grow." And «باسِقاتٍ» is a ḥāl, an anticipated one (muqaddara), since at the time of their growth they were not tall. «البُسُوْقُ» is height. One says «بَسَقَ فلانٌ على أصحابِه», that is, he towered over his companions in excellence. From it is the saying of Ibn Nawfal about Ibn Hubayra: 4091 - يا بنَ الذين بمَجْدِهمْ ... بَسَقَتْ على قَيْسٍ فَزارَهْ
(O son of those by whose glory Fazāra towered over Qays.)
It is a metaphor; the original usage is in «بَسَقَتِ النخلةُ تَبْسُق بُسُوْقاً», that is, it grew tall. The poet said:
4092 - لنا خَمْرٌ وليسَتْ خمرَ كَرْمٍ ... ولكنْ مِنْ نِتاجِ الباسِقاتِ
كِرامٌ في السماءِ ذَهَبْنَ طُوْلاً ... وفاتَ ثمارَها أيدي الجُناةِ
(We have wine, though not the wine of vines, but from the produce of the tall palms: noble ones that went up high in the sky, their fruit beyond the hands of the pickers.)
«بَسَقَتِ الشاةُ» means the ewe gave birth; «أَبْسَقَت الناقةُ» means the colostrum came into her udder before delivery, and from that «نوقٌ مَباسِيْقُ». The majority read it with sīn. Qutba ibn Mālik, who reports it from the Prophet ﷺ, read «باصِقاتٍ» with ṣād, which is a dialect of Banū l-ʿAnbar, who replace sīn with ṣād before qāf, ghayn, khāʾ and ṭāʾ when these follow it, or are separated from it by one or two letters.
His saying: {لَّهَا طَلْعٌ نَّضِيدٌ}: the sentence may be a ḥāl from «النخل» or from the pronoun in «باسِقاتٍ»; it may also be that the ḥāl is «لها» alone, with «طَلْعٌ» its agent, and «نَضِيْدٌ» in the sense of «مَنْضود» (stacked).

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {رِّزْقاً}: it may be a ḥāl, that is, "provision for the servants", i.e. possessing provision; it may be a maṣdar from the meaning of «أَنْبَتْنا», because the growing of this is provision; and it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. And «للعباد» is either an adjective, or attached to the maṣdar, or an object of the maṣdar with a redundant lām, that is: "provision for the servants."
His saying: {بِهِ}: that is, with the water. And «مَيْتاً» is an adjective of «بَلْدة». It was not made feminine, considering the meaning of place. The majority read it light. Abū Jaʿfar and Khālid read it heavy.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {الأيكة}: it has been discussed in al-Shuʿarāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read it here as «لَيْكَة» on the pattern of «لَيْلَة». The Shaykh said: "Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Ṭalḥa and Nāfiʿ read «الأَيْكةِ» with the definite lām, and the majority «لَيْكَة»." What he reported is a lapse of his; rather the well-known disagreement is only in Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ and Ṣād, as I verified there; but here the majority read it with the definite lām.
His saying: {كُلٌّ}: the tanwīn is a replacement for the omitted muḍāf ilayhi. Some grammarians allowed dropping its tanwīn and making it indeclinable on ḍamma, as the majority do with «قبل» and «بعد».

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {أَفَعَيِينَا}: the majority read it with a yāʾ with kasra followed by a quiescent yāʾ. Its meaning has already passed in al-Aḥqāf. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «أفَعَيِّنا» with the yāʾ doubled without lengthening. This reading, for all its difficulty, was read by al-Walīd ibn Muslim, Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and Nāfiʿ in one transmission, and Ibn Khālawayh reported from Ibn Abī ʿAbla «أفَعَيِّينا» likewise, but he brought a further quiescent yāʾ after the doubled yāʾ. The Shaykh explained it on the dialect of those who say «عَيِيَ» → «عَيَّ», and «حَيِيَ» → «حَيَّ», with assimilation. Then, when this verb is predicated while assimilated, and the dialect of Bakr ibn Wāʾil is taken into account, namely that they do not undo the assimilation in such a case when they predicate the assimilated verb to the speaker's tāʾ, or any of its sisters for which the lām of the verb becomes quiescent, so they say of «رَدَّ»: «رَدْتُ» and «رَدْنا», he said: "on this dialect / the yāʾ is with fatḥa." I say: he did not mention the justification of the other reading. Its justification is that it is from «عَيَّا يُعَيِّي» like «حَلَّى يُحَلِّي».

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {وَنَعْلَمُ}: the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "and We know"; the nominal sentence is then a ḥāl. It cannot be a ḥāl by itself, because it is an affirmative imperfect directly preceded by the wāw. Likewise His saying «ونحن أقربُ».
His saying: {مِنْ حَبْلِ الوريد}: this is like their saying «مسجد الجامع», that is, the cord of the jugular vein; or because «الحبل» is more general, to clarify, as in «بعير سانية»; or the cord of the shoulder (ʿātiq) is intended, and so it is annexed to the vein as it is annexed to the shoulder, because both are in one limb. «الوريد» is either in the sense of «الوارد» or in the sense of «المورود». «الوريد» is a large vein in the neck; it is said that there are two jugular veins. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Two veins enclosing the two sides of the neck at the front, joined to the aorta (watīn); they come down from the head to it. It is called warīd because the spirit comes (tarid) to it." And he recited:
4093 - كأنْ وَرِيْدَيْهِ رِشاءُ خُلْبِ
(As if his two jugular veins were a rope of palm fibre.)
al-Athram said: "It is the river of the body: in the heart it is the watīn, in the back the abhar, in the arm and thigh the akḥal and the nasā, and in the little finger the aslam."

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {إِذْ يَتَلَقَّى}: an adverbial of «أَقْرَبُ». It may also be accusative by "remember".
His saying: {عَنِ اليمين وَعَنِ الشمال قَعِيدٌ}: it may be singular on its usual sense, so it means «مُفاعِل» like «خليط» in the sense of «مُخالِط»; or it may be shifted from «فاعِل» to «فعيل» for intensity, like «عليم». The Kufans allowed «فعيل» to stand in the place of two. al-Mubarrad said: "The original is: 'on the right a sitter and on the left'; so it was postponed from its place." This does not escape the singular standing in the place of the dual. The better course is to claim an omission, either from the first, that is: "on the right a sitter and on the left a sitter", or from the second, so that the pronounced «قعيدٌ» belongs to the first. Similar is the saying of another:
4094 - رَماني بأَمْرٍ كنتُ منه ووالدي ... بَريئاً ومِنْ أجل الطَّوِيِّ رَماني
(He accused me of a matter of which I and my father were innocent, and on account of the well he accused me.)

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {مَّا يَلْفِظُ}: the majority read it with kasra on the fāʾ, and Muḥammad ibn Abī Maʿdān with fatḥa. «رقيبٌ عتيدٌ» is said to mean «رقيبان عتيدان» (two watchers, ready).

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {بالحق}: the bāʾ may be of ḥāl, that is, "joined with the truth", and it may be of transitivity. ʿAbd Allāh read «سَكَراتُ». «تَحيد» means "you incline", from «حادَ عن الشيء يَحيد حُيُوداً وحُيُوْدَة وحَيْداً».

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {مَّعَهَا سَآئِقٌ}: a sentence in the genitive position as an adjective of «نَفْسٍ», or in the nominative as an adjective of «كل», or in the accusative as a ḥāl from «كلُّ». The majority read «معها» without assimilation; Ṭalḥa read it with assimilation, «مَحَّا» with a doubled ḥāʾ; that is, he assimilated the ʿayn into the hāʾ, which is not possible, so he turned the hāʾ into ḥāʾ, then assimilated the ʿayn into it, turning it into ḥāʾ. «ذَهَبَ مَحُّمْ», that is, «معهم», was heard. al-Zamakhsharī said: "The position of «معها سائقٌ» is accusative as ḥāl from «كلُّ», because it is made definite by annexation to what is in the status of a definite." The Shaykh attacked him, as is his habit, saying: "A beginner in grammar would not say this, because if «كلُّ نفس» were qualified, it would be qualified only by an indefinite." This is unbecoming of him, since he knows that he did not mean literally what he said.

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {لَّقَدْ كُنتَ}: that is, it is said to him: "You were indeed...", and the saying is either an adjective or a ḥāl. The majority read fatḥa on the tāʾ and the kāf in «كنتَ», «غِطاءَكَ» and «فبصَرُك», following the masculine wording of «كلُّ». al-Jaḥdarī read «كنتِ» with kasra, addressing the soul; he and Ṭalḥa ibn Muṣarrif read «عنكِ», «غطاءَكِ», «فبصَرُكِ» with kasra, also taking the soul into account. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» did not report the kasra of the kāf from al-Jaḥdarī; in sum, he took the wording into account in one place and the meaning in another.

semin-durr:23-23.t: His saying: {هذا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ}: «ما» may be an indefinite described noun, «عتيدٌ» its adjective, and «لَدَيَّ» attached to «عتيدٌ», that is: "this is a thing ready with me", i.e. present with me. On this «لديَّ» may be a description of «ما», with «عتيدٌ» a second adjective, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "it is ready." It may also be a relative noun meaning "that which"; «لَدَيَّ» is its ṣila and «عتيدٌ» the khabar of the relative, and the relative with its ṣila is the khabar of the demonstrative. It may also be that «ما» is a badal from «هذا», whether relative or described by «لَدَيَّ», with «عتيدٌ» the khabar of «هذا». al-Zamakhsharī allowed «عَتيدٌ» to be a badal, or a khabar after a khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. / The majority read it in the nominative; ʿAbd Allāh put it in the accusative as a ḥāl. The better course then is that «ما» be relative, because it is definite, and ḥāl often comes from a definite. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Had this occurred outside the Qurʾān, it would be permissible to put it in the accusative as a ḥāl." I say: what he wished has come, thanks be to Allah; it seems he did not come across it as a reading.

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {أَلْقِيَا}: they differed: is the one commanded one or two? Some said: one, and the dual pronoun was used to indicate repetition of the act, as if it were said: "Cast, cast." It is also said: he meant «أَلْقِيَنْ» with the light nūn, and replaced it with an alif, treating continuation like pause; this is supported by al-Ḥasan's reading «أَلْقِيَنْ» with the nūn.
It is also said: the Arabs address one person as they address two, for emphasis, as in:
4095 - فإن تَزْجُراني يا بنَ عَفَّانَ أَزْدَجِرْ ... وإنْ تَدَعاني أَحْمِ عِرْضاً مُمَنَّعا
(If you two rebuke me, O Ibn ʿAffān, I will desist; and if you two leave me alone, I will protect a well-guarded honour.)
And another said:
4096 - فقُلْتُ لصاحبي لا تَحْبِسانا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(I said to my companion: "Do not you two hold us back...")
the verse. Some said: the one commanded is a dual. This is the truth, because what is meant is two angels who do that.

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {الذي جَعَلَ}: it may be accusative for censure, or as a badal from «كل»; or genitive as a badal from «كَفَّار»; or nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with «فَأَلْقياه» as the khabar. It is said that the fāʾ entered because of its likeness to a condition. It may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is: "he is the one who made", and «فَأَلْقِياه» would then be an emphasis. Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed it to be an adjective of «الكَفَّار», saying: "inasmuch as «كَفَّار» is specific to the mentioned attributes, it is permissible to qualify it with this definite." This is rejected. It was also read with fatḥa on the tanwīn, to avoid the succession of four similar letters.

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {قَالَ قَرِينُهُ}: this came without a wāw because resumption is intended by it, as if the disbeliever had said: "My Lord, he made me transgress", and his companion said: "I did not make him transgress"; unlike the one before it, which is conjoined to what precedes it to indicate the combination of its meaning and the meaning of what precedes in occurrence, I mean the coming of «كلُّ نفس» with the two angels and the saying of his companion what he said to him.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {قَالَ لاَ تَخْتَصِمُواْ}: also resumptive, as if someone asked: "What did Allah say to him?" and it was answered: «قال: لا تَخْتصموا».
His saying: {وَقَدْ قَدَّمْتُ}: a ḥāl clause. It requires interpretation, for the prohibition is in the Hereafter and the advance warning was in the world, so the two times differ; how then can it be made a ḥāl? Its interpretation is that the meaning is "and it has been established that I gave advance warning", and the time of establishment and the time of the prohibition are the same. «قَدَّمْتُ» may be in the sense of «تَقَدَّمْتُ», so the tāʾ is of ḥāl, and a muḍāf must be omitted, that is: "and My word to you has preceded, joined with the warning." It may also be that «قَدَّمْتُ» is transitive as it is, with the bāʾ redundant in the object, that is: "I gave you advance warning of the threat."

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ نَقُولُ}: «يوم» is accusative, either by «ظَلاَّم», but this has no implication, because if He does not wrong on this day, the negation of wrong on other days is all the more so; or by His saying {وَنُفِخَ فِي الصور} [Qāf: 20], the pointing "that" referring to «يومَ نقول»; said by al-Zamakhsharī, and the Shaykh found it remote because of the many intervening elements; or by an implied "remember", or by "warn", and on these last two it is a direct object, not an adverbial.
His saying: {هَلْ مِن مَّزِيدٍ}: a question of affirmation and making them stand to account. It is also said: its meaning is negation. It is also said: the question is put to its keepers, and the answer is from them, so a muḍāf must be omitted, that is: "We say to the keepers of Hell, and they say", then he omitted it. Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr read «يقول لجهنمَ» with the third-person yāʾ, the agent being Allah the Exalted, since He was mentioned earlier in His saying «مع الله»; the others read with the nūn of the speaker glorifying himself, since He was mentioned earlier in «لديَّ» and «وقد قَدَّمْتُ». al-Aʿmash read «يُقال» as a passive. «المزيد» may be a maṣdar, and may be a passive participle, that is: "Is there anything you add for Me that I might burn?"

ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ق وَالْقُرْآنِ الْمَجِيدِ (١) بَلْ عَجِبُوا أَنْ جَاءَهُمْ مُنْذِرٌ مِنْهُمْ فَقَالَ الْكَافِرُونَ هَذَا شَيْءٌ عَجِيبٌ (٢) أَئِذَا مِتْنَا وَكُنَّا تُرَابًا ذَلِكَ رَجْعٌ بَعِيدٌ (٣)).
Whoever says that (ق) is an oath makes the wāw in (وَالْقُرْآنِ) a conjunction; for whoever says otherwise, it is the wāw of the oath. The apodosis of the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is omitted. It is said that it is His saying: (قَدْ عَلِمْنَا . . . (٤)), i.e. لَقَدْ, the lām having been dropped because of the length of the speech.
It is also said that it is omitted, its implied form being "you will surely be resurrected" (لَتُبْعَثُنَّ) or "you will surely be returned" (لَتُرْجَعُنَّ), according to what the context of the verses indicates.
And (بَلْ) is for moving from one story to another. And (إِذَا) is accusative by what the answer indicates, i.e. "shall we return?"

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ الْوَرِيدِ (١٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَنَعْلَمُ), i.e. "while We know", so the clause is a ḥāl muqaddara (anticipated circumstantial). It may also be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:17-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذْ يَتَلَقَّى الْمُتَلَقِّيَانِ عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَعَنِ الشِّمَالِ قَعِيدٌ (١٧) مَا يَلْفِظُ مِنْ قَوْلٍ إِلَّا لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ (١٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ يَتَلَقَّى) may be an adverb (ẓarf) for أَقْرَبُ, or the implied wording may be "remember".
And (قَعِيدٌ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «عَنِ الشِّمَالِ» is its khabar (predicate); this «قَعِيدٌ» indicates the first «قَعِيدٌ», i.e. "on the right is one seated".
It is also said that the «قَعِيدٌ» mentioned is the first, and the second is omitted.
It is also said that there is no omission: قَعِيدٌ means "two seated ones", the singular sufficing for the dual; parallels to this have passed before. And (رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌ) is singular in wording, while the meaning is "two watchers, ready".

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الْمَوْتِ بِالْحَقِّ ذَلِكَ مَا كُنْتَ مِنْهُ تَحِيدُ (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِالْحَقِّ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

ukberi-tibyan:21-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَعَهَا سَائِقٌ وَشَهِيدٌ (٢١) لَقَدْ كُنْتَ فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هَذَا فَكَشَفْنَا عَنْكَ غِطَاءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ الْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَعَهَا سَائِقٌ): the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of نَفْس, or of كُلّ, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from كُلّ; this is permissible because of the generality in it. And the implied wording is: "it will be said to him: لَقَدْ كُنْتَ …", the masculine being used according to the meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَقَالَ قَرِينُهُ هَذَا مَا لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَذَا) is a mubtadaʾ (subject). Regarding «مَا» there are two views. First: it is indefinite, and «عَتِيدٌ» is its adjective (ṣifa), and «لَدَيَّ» is governed by عَتِيد.
«لَدَيَّ» may also be an adjective too, so it is attached to something omitted; and «مَا» with its adjective is the khabar (predicate) of هَذَا.
The second view: «مَا» means "that which" (al-ladhī); on this view «مَا» is a mubtadaʾ, «لَدَيَّ» is the ṣila (relative clause), «عَتِيدٌ» is the khabar of «مَا», and the clause is the khabar of «هَذَا». «مَا» may also be a badal (substitute) for هَذَا.
«عَتِيدٌ» may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, with «مَا لَدَيَّ» being the khabar of «هَذَا», i.e. "it is ready". Had that occurred outside the Quran, its accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) would have been permissible.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفَّارٍ عَنِيدٍ (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَلْقِيَا), i.e. that will be said. Regarding the dual form here there are several views. First: it is an address to the two angels. Second: it is to one, and the alif is a substitute for repeating the verb, i.e. "throw, throw" (أَلْقِ أَلْقِ).
Third: it is to one, but it came out in the dual form according to their custom, as in their sayings خَلِيلِيَّ عُوجَا ("my two friends, turn aside") and خَلِيلِيَّ مُرَّا بِي ("my two friends, pass by me with me"); that is because the usual state of one of them is that two companions accompany him on a journey. Fourth: some of the Arabs address one person with the address of two, as in the poet's saying:
فَإِنْ تَزْجُرَانِي يَا بْنَ عَفَّانَ أَنْزَجِرْ ... وَإِنْ تَدَعَانِي أَحْمِ عِرْضًا مُمَنَّعًا
(If you [two] restrain me, O son of ʿAffān, I will be restrained; and if you [two] leave me, I will defend an honour well protected.)
Fifth: the alif is a substitute for the light nūn (of emphasis), and the connected (speech) was treated like the pause.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَنَّاعٍ لِلْخَيْرِ مُعْتَدٍ مُرِيبٍ الَّذِي جَعَلَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَهًا آخَرَ فَأَلْقِيَاهُ فِي الْعَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ (٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُرِيبٍ الَّذِي): the majority read the tanwīn with kasra. It has also been read with fatḥa, to escape the (succession of) kasras and the yāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:31-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأُزْلِفَتِ الْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ (٣١) هَذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ لِكُلِّ أَوَّابٍ حَفِيظٍ (٣٢)).
(غَيْرَ بَعِيدٍ), i.e. "at a place not far".
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْجَنَّة; it was not made feminine because "garden", "orchard" and "abode" are close in meaning.
And (هَذَا مَا تُوعَدُونَ): the implied wording is "it will be said to them: هَذَا …". The yāʾ in «تُوعَدُونَ» is for the third person, and the tāʾ is for returning to the address.

ukberi-tibyan:33-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَنْ خَشِيَ الرَّحْمَنَ بِالْغَيْبِ وَجَاءَ بِقَلْبٍ مُنِيبٍ (٣٣) ادْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَامٍ ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُلُودِ (٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ خَشِيَ) is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "they are those who feared"; or in the position of the genitive as a badal (substitute) for «الْمُتَّقِينَ» or for «كُلِّ أَوَّابٍ»; or in the position of the accusative, i.e. "I mean those who feared".
It is also said that «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "it will be said to them: enter it".
And (بِسَلَامٍ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ), i.e. "the time of that is «يَوْمُ الْخُلُودِ»".

ukberi-tibyan:35-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَهُمْ مَا يَشَاءُونَ فِيهَا وَلَدَيْنَا مَزِيدٌ (٣٥) وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَشَدُّ مِنْهُمْ بَطْشًا فَنَقَّبُوا فِي الْبِلَادِ هَلْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ (٣٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِيهَا) may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَشَاءُونَ, or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَا» or from the omitted referent pronoun. And (كَمْ) is accusative by «أَهْلَكْنَا». And (هُمْ أَشَدُّ) may be genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of قَرْن, or accusative as an adjective of كَمْ.
The fāʾ entered «فَنَقَّبُوا» as a conjunction according to the meaning, i.e. "they were mighty in assault, and so they roamed"; there are readings in it whose meaning is clear. The meaning is: "is there for them", or "is there for whoever follows their path".
(مِنْ مَحِيصٍ), i.e. "any refuge"; the khabar (predicate) was omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:40-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَارَ السُّجُودِ (٤٠) وَاسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنَادِي الْمُنَادِي مِنْ مَكَانٍ قَرِيبٍ (٤١) يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ الصَّيْحَةَ بِالْحَقِّ ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ الْخُرُوجِ (٤٢) إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي وَنُمِيتُ وَإِلَيْنَا الْمَصِيرُ (٤٣) يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ الْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعًا ذَلِكَ حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌ (٤٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَدْبَارَ السُّجُودِ): with fatḥa on the hamza, the plural of دُبُر; and with kasra on it, the maṣdar (verbal noun) of أَدْبَرَ, the implied wording being "at the time of the ending of prostration". And (يَوْمَ يَسْمَعُونَ) is a badal (substitute) for «يَوْمَ يُنَادِي». And (يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ) is an adverb (ẓarf) for الْمَصِير, or a badal for the first يَوْمَ. And (سِرَاعًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "they come out hastening".
«يَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ» may also be an adverb for this implied (verb). And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:6-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَلَمْ يَنْظُرُوا إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَوْقَهُمْ كَيْفَ بَنَيْنَاهَا وَزَيَّنَّاهَا وَمَا لَهَا مِنْ فُرُوجٍ (٦) وَالْأَرْضَ مَدَدْنَاهَا وَأَلْقَيْنَا فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ وَأَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ (٧) تَبْصِرَةً وَذِكْرَى لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُنِيبٍ (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَوْقَهُمْ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السَّمَاء, or an adverb (ẓarf) for يَنْظُرُوا.
And (الْأَرْضُ) [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the analysis that follows treats it as accusative, الْأَرْضَ] is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the position of السَّمَاء, i.e. "and they see the earth"; on this view «مَدَدْنَاهَا» is a ḥāl.
It may also be accusative on the implied wording "and We spread out the earth".
And (تَبْصِرَةً) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a ḥāl from the object, i.e. "possessing insight-giving"; or a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "We gave them insight". (وَذِكْرَى) likewise.

ukberi-tibyan:9-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَنَزَّلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً مُبَارَكًا فَأَنْبَتْنَا بِهِ جَنَّاتٍ وَحَبَّ الْحَصِيدِ (٩) وَالنَّخْلَ بَاسِقَاتٍ لَهَا طَلْعٌ نَضِيدٌ (١٠) رِزْقًا لِلْعِبَادِ وَأَحْيَيْنَا بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتًا كَذَلِكَ الْخُرُوجُ (١١)).
